steps.content:
The cause is instance family **oAYMdj0PDJ** (cloud service a7YTm, application nI7). It runs at a fixed price of 0.4, so its cost goes up and down only with how many instances are running.

1. **It drove most of the jump.** Account e0yOWue's total daily cost rose from about $8,122 on 2025-10-12 to $8,499 on 2025-10-13, an increase of about $377. This instance family went from 6 to 36 instances, so its cost rose from $57.60 to $345.60. That $288 rise is about three quarters of the account's increase. The next largest rise was family vQexwxMSgl, at about $66.
2. **It has also been growing week over week.** Both families scale up on Mondays and back down later in the week. vQexwxMSgl returns to the same Monday level each week (21 instances, $69.05), so I treated it as routine. oAYMdj0PDJ climbs each week instead. Its Monday peak went from 30 instances ($288) to 33 ($316.80) to 36 ($345.60) over the last three weeks. Compared with the previous Monday (2025-10-06), it had the largest increase of any instance family, at $28.80.

One caveat: the account's total on 2025-10-13 ($8,499) was slightly below the previous Monday ($8,545). Much of the day-over-day jump is therefore the normal Monday scale-up. The part that stands out as abnormal is this family's steady weekly growth.
